shortDescription: West African crude oil differentials were largely unchanged on Wednesday while the market faced increased crude supply disruptions in the Middle East.

children: West African crude oil differentials were largely unchanged on Wednesday while the market faced increased crude supply disruptions in the Middle East.
The market was quiet, a trader said, while others this week mentioned that high freight rates were putting downward pressure on demand.

Indian Oil Corp bought 4 million barrels of crude from the Middle East and Africa for November arrival in a tender, trade sources said, comprising of a million barrels each of Iraqi Basrah Heavy, Libyan Sarir/Messla, Angolan Cabinda and Nigerian Utapate grades.

In the wider market, Saudi Arabia cut oil shipments to Europe after drone attacks damaged its export pipeline to the Red Sea, trade sources told Reuters. Customers such as Poland have turned to the spot market to cover the shortfall, with the country buying nearly 16 million barrels of crude for its refineries.
